   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison/ Next Beverly Hills Committee

FROM:  Gabriella Yap, Senior Policy and Management Administrator

DATE:  April 19, 2023

SUBJECT:  Discussion of Next Beverly Hills Committee’s Proposed FY 2023-24 Work
  Plan and Budget
ATTACHMENTS  None

The purpose of this memo is to request review and approval of the Next Beverly Hills
Committee (Committee) proposed Fiscal Year 2023-24 work plan by the Beverly Hills City
Council Liaison/Next Beverly Hills Committee, consisting of Mayor Julian A. Gold, M.D. and Vice
Mayor Les Friedman.

INTRODUCTION
Next BH was established in 2015 to engage residents through innovative initiatives that address
their lifestyles, economic and civic needs, and to inspire them to make Beverly Hills a better
place for all. Next BH is a committee of talented, next generation leaders focused on innovative
initiatives which address the lifestyle, economic, and civic needs of those in their 20s, 30s, and
40s. Chartered by the Mayor and the City of Beverly Hills, it seeks to engage all who are
interested to inspire them to make Beverly Hills a better place for all.

At the transition of each calendar year, the Committee members select their leadership and
Priority Areas for the coming calendar year. Once the Priority Areas are selected, the
Committee may generate initiatives and projects for the calendar year if they fall within at least
one of the selected Priority Areas. Continuing initiatives and projects must also fall within at
least one of the selected Priority Areas.

For calendar year 2023, the Next BH leadership is as follows:

  •  Noah Etessami – Chair
  •  Charles Smith – Vice Chair
  •  Kipton Cronkite - Art Chair
  •  Joel Hile - Cultural Chair
  •  Allison Adams - Charity Chair
  •  Ariel Ouziel - Sustainability Chair

In addition, the City Council Liaisons, Mayor Gold and Vice Mayor Friedman, provide updates
on civic issues to bring awareness to the Next BH membership.
 For calendar year 2023, the Next BH Priority Areas are as follows:

  •  Leadership Development
  •  Next Gen Events & Outreach
  •  Next Gen Arts & Culture
  •  Historical Appreciation
  •  Cultural Unity
  •  Sustainability
  •  Safety & Quality of Life
  •  Charitable Engagement

DISCUSSION
The Committee is requesting Liaisons Mayor Gold and Vice Mayor Friedman review and
approve the proposed Next BH Work Plan and Budget for FY 23-24, as well as additional
budget and appropriation for FY 22-23 to begin work on the 2023 Next Night Street Festival. If
approved, the Committee will bring the work plan to the full City Council for approval.

Membership and Community Engagement Activities (Continued - $15,000)
Previously, Next BH had allocated $10,000 toward First Thursdays to promote community
engagement and increase patronage of local businesses during Covid and $5,000 toward
Membership Outreach. As part of First Thursdays, Next BH worked in partnership with the
Chamber of Commerce’s Now Beverly Hills campaign and with Concerts on Canon to cross-
promote the events and businesses. Additionally, Next Beverly Hills hosted events like garden
games in Beverly Canon Gardens and Guac with a Cop. First Thursdays concluded with a
successful last event in December 2022 as the Covid local emergency was tapering off.
Next Beverly Hills is proposing to pivot from the Covid-borne First Thursdays to general
activities to promote community engagement. Next Beverly Hills serves as an excellent entry
point into community involvement by being accessible to those who want to learn more about
the City and encourages member participation in the committee and other City programs. Some
activities Next BH is proposing would include monthly yoga at Greystone mansion, continuing
mixers with public safety departments and including other City initiatives like Just in Case BH,
and exploring partnering with UCLA and USC Film Schools and next gen college students to
exhibit films, utilize the beautiful theatre at Greystone, and expose them to our amazing city.
Next BH also recognizes that the people highly invested in the next generation are parents and
students, and the Committee is looking forward to hosting events to engage with a wide
segment of future generations including the:
  • Parent Teacher Association (PTA) to explore early education
  • School Board members to speak with the Committee to understand what is important to
  parents and families
  • High school students to hear what they are experiencing and want to see in Beverly Hills
  • School Principals to see how Next BH could partner with the schools
  • People who have moved back to Beverly Hills (or never left) to understand what draws
  them here. Is there anything they missed from their childhood here? Anything they were
  pleasantly surprised to see?

  2 of 5
 commUNITY Cultural Unity Initiative (Continued - $20,000)
The goal of Next’s Cultural Unity Initiative titled commUNITY is to involve the next generation
and encourage greater unity through diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Committee recognizes
the importance of celebrating our differences and what we each have to offer. As part of FY 22-
23, Next BH co-sponsored Festival BH, which celebrated the City’s rich diversity, and brought
together different segments of the community. Additionally, Next BH co-sponsored a screening
event at the Greystone Mansion Theatre with the Finnish Film Festival Midsummer in
Hollywood, who funded the event. Attendees included members of the Finnish Consulate,
Finnish and Swedish Chambers of Commerce, a variety of professionals in the entertainment
industry, alongside the public. Our members have expressed interest in similar partnerships in
the future. Next BH has enjoyed collaborating with staff and other commissions on events like
Festival BH and Beverly Hills PRIDE, and requests the same level of funding to continue the
goal of greater diversity, equity, and inclusion. This funding would go toward co-sponsoring
events, speaking panels, and other events that encourage unity.

Art Initiatives (Continued - $2,000)
Next BH has enjoyed success partnering with the Arts & Culture Commission and the Human
Relations Commission on Visions of the Future, and look forward to encouraging next-gen
interest in art at events such as the Art Show booths each year. In FY 22-23, Next BH
participated in the Art Shows, went on Art Walks, and also toured the Mr. Brainwash exhibit.
Funds were also used toward the giant community mural at Next Night as an additional
interactive activity.

Sustainability Initiatives (Continued - $2,000)
The goal of the Sustainability Initiatives is to prioritize sustainability for the next generation, in
particular related to climate change, recycling and resource conservation. Next BH requests
funding to continue working with the Public Works Department to host a Next BH booth at the
Farmer's Market, Earth Day events, and other City events where appropriate to showcase
sustainable products and next-gen ideas for encouraging sustainability, in addition to partnering
to create workshops and discussions to educate and encourage sustainable practices.
Additionally, Next BH previously held a clothing drive as both a sustainability and charitable
effort to encourage clothing recycling to benefit youth aging out of foster care. With the help of
the Fire Department, Next BH was able to donate a number of bags of clothing to foster youth.
Unusable clothing was sent to be recycled, diverting this potential waste from landfills. Funding
would be used toward similar sustainability initiatives.

Marketing (Continued - $5,000)
Next BH plans to utilize marketing funds in conjunction with the proposed initiatives approved by
the Council. This includes advertisements, various media channels, and Next BH branded
merchandise for events throughout the year.

Miscellaneous (Continued - $1,000)
Miscellaneous costs for services and supplies such as a SurveyMonkey subscription.

  3 of 5
 Next Night Street Festival ($230,000 = $200,000 with 10% Contingency))
In October 2022, after a hiatus due to COVID-19, the Next Night Street Festival returned and we
saw an unprecedented 5,000 people show up for this event. The goal of Next Night will continue
to be creating a street festival with live entertainment, food, and games which appeal to the next
generation of Beverly Hills residents while encouraging the entire community to come together
and celebrate life in Beverly Hills. The kids area was extremely popular last year and it is
recommended that we enlarge the kids zone and add additional children’s elements for this
year’s Next Night. Additionally, Next BH and the community greatly enjoyed partnering with the
school district and the Teen Advisory Committee and will be looking forward to doing so again.
This year’s Next Night is proposed to take place on Saturday, September 9, 2023.

Due to the increasing cost of labor, manufacturing items, and supply chain challenges, the total
cost of the last event was approximately $210,000 when combining the event elements, event
management services, talent costs, and supplies and services such as fencing, porta-potties
and k-rails. This did not include soft costs which include, but are not limited to, the use of City
staff and resources associated with the event and a full street closure, security, marketing and
advertisement, printing and graphics, and waiving permits and parking fees. For FY 2022-23,
the Council approved an ongoing budget enhancement of $150,000 for Next Night. Due to the
increase in costs consistent across all proposals received. Next is requesting an additional
annual appropriation of $80,000 to cover the event costs, including a 10% contingency of
$20,000, as well as Council approval to close the street and inclusion of soft costs discussed
above.

FISCAL IMPACT

Next BH’s FY 22-23 base budget allocation was $185,000. This amount included $150,000
budgeted for Next Night and $35,000 for ongoing activities. Upon receiving the Next Night event
proposals which all reflected higher costs in a post-Covid world, the Next BH Committee
returned to the Council for an additional appropriation of $42,900 for the event management
services alone. As discussed above, Next Night costs were closer to $210,000 when taking into
account all costs like talent, k-rails, porta potties, and fencing. This does not include the staff
and resources related to the event and a full street closure, security, marketing and
advertisement, printing and graphics, and waiving permits and parking fees.
Waiting for the next year’s budget has always presented time challenges for the group in being
able to enter into and pay agreements related to Next Night, and will present more challenges
given the earlier proposed date of September 9, 2023. In order to enable Next BH to begin
planning the 2023 Next Night earlier, Next BH is asking the Council to consider approving an FY
22-23 additional budget and appropriation in the amount of $230,000 ($210,000 with $20,000
contingency) to begin work and to carryover funds as needed.

The FY 22-23 Membership Outreach and Cultural Unity Initiatives were funded from carryover
funds last year and an appropriation of $15,000 is requested in FY 23-24. Next BH is also
requesting an additional $80,000 in the FY 23-24 budget and appropriation for Next Night into
the Business Development budget (00101313-734200) for the 2024 Next Night. Below is a table
showing the existing budget and requests.

23-24 work plan along with the corresponding budget and appropriation requests for FY 22-23
and FY 23-24.
